title: Coefficient change preserves the clopen-normalized refinement mate
statement:
Let $X,T_1,T_2$ be schemes, let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper, and let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be quasi-compact open immersions with $uj_1=j_2$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On the small pro-etale site of $T_2$ choose a homomorphism $a:A\to B$ of sheaves of commutative rings; on $T_1,X$ use the inverse images of both coefficient sheaves and the coefficient map. Use ordinary unbounded derived module categories and K-flat scalar extension $S_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Use the canonical derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions and exact open extension [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].

Put $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, with projections $b:V\to T_1$, $q:V\to X$, and clopen section $s=(j_1,1_X):X\to V$. For $D=A,B$, let $\pi_s^D:N\to s_!s^{-1}N$ be identity on $s(X)$ and zero on the complementary open. With the open-unit-normalized base-change map $\beta_D:u_D^{-1}j_{2!,D}\cong b_{!,D}q_D^{-1}$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], set
$$h_D:u_D^{-1}j_{2!,D}\xrightarrow{\beta_D}b_{!,D}q_D^{-1}\xrightarrow{b_{!,D}\pi_s^Dq_D^{-1}}b_{!,D}s_{!,D}s_D^{-1}q_D^{-1}\cong j_{1!,D}.$$
Define the refinement transformation $r_D:j_{2!,D}\to Ru_{*,D}j_{1!,D}$ to be the $u_D^{-1}\dashv Ru_{*,D}$-adjunct of $h_D$. Let $\delta_i:S_{T_i}j_{i!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{i!,B}S_X$ be the normalized open scalar comparison [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Let $\chi_u:S_{T_2}Ru_{*,A}\to Ru_{*,B}S_{T_1}$ be the $B$-linear counit transpose of the canonical inverse-image/scalar comparison, as in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. For every $M\in D(A_X)$ one has the equality in $D(B_{T_2})$
$$Ru_{*,B}(\delta_{1,M})\circ\chi_{u,j_{1!,A}M}\circ S_{T_2}(r_{A,M})=r_{B,S_XM}\circ\delta_{2,M}.$$
The equation is natural in $M$, in the coefficient homomorphism and in successive proper refinements under canonical direct-image composition; it commutes with cochain shifts. It requires no flatness or invertibility of $\chi_u$ and no cartesian hypothesis on $uj_1=j_2$.

All constructions and the displayed equation also apply to compatible maps $A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ of strict inverse coefficient systems, using the ordinary ringed diagram topoi [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. They then hold as transformations on the whole derived categories of systems before evaluation, total limit, or restriction to normalized inputs. In the constant finite-ring case, $r_D$ is the normalized refinement map of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus].
